title: Perf Canary (Prod) Kickoff Notes — working doc
body:
Doc purpose
- Scratchpad from kickoff + early follow-ups.
- Capture: goals, initial scope, owners, open questions, model coverage v0, early links (dashboards/queries), and decision log (lightweight).

Meeting(s)
- 2025-12-02 Perf Canary kickoff (runtime + SRE + telemetry + product rollouts)
- 2025-12-04 follow-up on baseline strategy + label/cardinality review

Attendees (partial)
- Runtime: Noah (TL), Sofia (scheduler), Hiro (kernels), Omar (instrumentation)
- Bench/evals: Rina (synthetic prompts)
- Telemetry/obs: Logan (telemetry platform), Nadia (baselines), Allison (alerting standards)
- SRE/oncall: Sean (SRE sponsor), Rafael (routing/incident bot)
- Product/release: Marissa (product owner), Connor (release gates)

High-level goal (as aligned)
- Always-on synthetic workload in prod that catches regressions before customers feel it.
- Primary signals per model: p95 latency + tokens/sec (plus breakdowns to attribute root cause: kernel vs scheduler vs infra).
- Minimal overhead: target <0.5% GPU capacity per region for covered models.
- Strict privacy: synthetic prompts only; no customer prompts; no PII; no customer identifiers.

MVP scope (phase 1)
- Start in us-east only.
- 2–3 models only.
- Warning-level alerts only for first week(s); paging after thresholds stabilize.
- Dashboards must be usable by oncall (fast “is this real?” + “where is time going?”).

Non-goals for MVP
- Shadowing customer traffic (explicitly out).
- Deep quality eval coupling (handled by eval harness separately).

Workstream owners (working)
- perf-canary service skeleton + request loop: Noah
- Scheduler attribution metrics (queueing/batch size): Sofia + Omar
- Kernel tagging (kernel selection/version): Hiro + Omar
- Synthetic prompt distribution + generator: Rina
- Metrics schema + cardinality guardrails: Logan + Allison
- Baseline store + evaluator: Nadia
- Dashboards + alerting rules + incident-bot formatting: Allison + Rafael
- Rollout gates integration: Connor + Marissa

What we think “good” looks like
- Detects 10–15% p95 regression within ~15–30 mins with low noise.
- Detects 10–20% tokens/sec drop within ~15–30 mins.
- Alert payload has enough context to answer:
  - Which model/version? which runtime build? which kernel id? which region/SKU?
  - Is queueing up vs execution up?
  - Is batch size distribution shifting?
  - Is there a matching infra event (fleet rollout, node type change)?

Definitions (working, subject to change)
- e2e latency: client send -> server response completed (incl queueing + execution + network inside region).
- runtime latency: queueing + GPU execution + post-processing (excludes client overhead).
- prefill latency: time to process prompt tokens.
- decode latency: time per generated token (or time to generate N tokens).
- tokens/sec: output tokens / total request time (define exactly for streaming; likely decode-only tokens/sec AND end-to-end tokens/sec).

Initial model coverage list (v0)
NOTE: names below are the canonical registry names we expect to see in telemetry. If registry aliases differ, Quentin to confirm canonical mapping.

Phase 1 candidates (us-east)
- Option A (top-of-funnel + common):
  - llama-3.1-70b-instruct (high volume, sensitive to batching)
  - qwen2.5-72b-instruct (recent kernel work; watch for regressions)
- Option B (add one more for shape diversity):
  - llama-3.1-8b-instruct (fast model; catches scheduler/queueing weirdness)

High-risk list (phase 2 add)
- Newly onboarded models (first 2 weeks post-launch)
- Models with active kernel experimentation flags
- Models with frequent config churn (rope scaling, kv-cache settings, quant profiles)

Open question: “top models” list source of truth
- Proposal: weekly export from model registry usage metrics -> maintained allowlist with manual overrides.
- Owner: Marissa + Quentin (partner) + Noah.

Synthetic workload (prompt shapes) — early proposal
- Goal: approximate production shape distribution without being too complex.
- v0 prompt buckets (token counts are approximate; we need to match tokenizer/model):
  - S: prompt 64–128, output 128
  - M: prompt 256–512, output 256
  - L: prompt 1k–2k, output 256
  - XL: prompt 4k–8k, output 128 (lower frequency)
- Mix: 35% S, 40% M, 20% L, 5% XL (tentative)
- Determinism: seedable generator; fixed set of shape-only prompts (no customer text).

Open questions / decisions needed
1) Baseline strategy
- Fixed baseline per (model, model_version, runtime_build, hardware_sku, region) vs rolling baseline.
- Concern: rolling baselines can “learn the regression” if it persists.
- Concern: fixed baselines drift with fleet changes / traffic mix changes.
- Proposed compromise (Nadia):
  - Baseline anchored to “last known good” build artifact + periodic re-baseline job on stable releases.
  - Rolling window only for variance estimation (not mean).
- Decision pending.

2) Dimensions (cardinality risk)
- MUST have: model, model_version, region
- STRONGLY want: runtime_build_id, kernel_id (or kernel_config hash), hardware_sku
- Maybe: tier (hosted vs dedicated) — only if we keep it small/controlled.
- Avoid: per-pod/per-node labels; request_id; prompt_bucket as label if too many.
- Action: telemetry label set review (Logan + Allison). Keep query patterns in mind.

3) Sampling + rate limits (overhead budget)
- Need explicit QPS caps per (region, model) and global cap.
- Need guardrails to prevent accidental fan-out to all models/regions.
- Proposal: control plane config with validation + audit log.
- Action: Noah to add config limiter + safe defaults.

4) What exactly triggers paging?
- Two-tier policy:
  - WARN: 10% p95 regression or 15% tok/s drop sustained 30 min, min N samples
  - PAGE: top models only; 15% p95 regression sustained 30–60 min AND min N samples; or 25% tok/s drop sustained 30 min
- Need anti-flap: dampening window + “must recover for X minutes” before auto-resolve.
- SRE request: paging only after we run warning-only for ~1–2 weeks.
- Action: Allison + Rafael draft policy; Sean approves.

5) Attribution signals (“is it kernel vs scheduler vs infra?”)
- Need to make sure we can answer with first dashboard view:
  - queueing_time increasing => likely scheduler/capacity
  - execution_time increasing + kernel_id changed => likely kernels
  - execution_time increasing + gpu clocks/thermals? => infra
  - batch size distribution shift => scheduler heuristics
- Action: Sofia/Omar confirm scheduler queueing metrics correctness.
- Action: Hiro/Omar confirm kernel_id tagging is stable and low cardinality.

6) Staging vs prod variance
- We expect higher variance in prod due to noisy neighbors, fleet heterogeneity, network, etc.
- Avoid setting thresholds based only on staging.
- Action: run “shadow-like” baseline jobs in prod but isolated capacity.

Early dashboard / query links (WIP)
- Grafana (WIP): Per-model perf canary overview
  - https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/perf-canary/perf-canary-overview?orgId=1
- Grafana (WIP): Attribution breakdown (queue vs runtime)
  - https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/perf-canary-attrib/perf-canary-attribution?orgId=1
- Honeycomb dataset (WIP): perf-canary traces
  - https://ui.honeycomb.io/redwood/datasets/perf-canary/overview
- PromQL snippets (rough; do not paste into prod alerts yet)
  - p95 e2e latency (model):
    - histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, model) (rate(perf_canary_request_latency_ms_bucket{region="us-east"}[10m])))
  - tokens/sec (model):
    - sum by (model) (rate(perf_canary_output_tokens_total{region="us-east"}[10m])) / sum by (model) (rate(perf_canary_request_latency_seconds_sum{region="us-east"}[10m]))
  - queueing time p95 (model):
    - histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, model) (rate(runtime_scheduler_queueing_ms_bucket{source="perf_canary",region="us-east"}[10m])))

NOTE: query names/metrics will change once Omar lands instrumentation + Logan signs off on schema.

Action items (next 1–2 weeks)
- [Noah] Write perf-canary service skeleton + config + request loop (ENG-4872). Target PR by 12/09.
- [Rina] Deliver synthetic prompt shape v0 + seedable generator (ENG-4872/PR perf-canary#19205). Target by 12/10.
- [Omar + Sofia] Export/validate queueing_time + batch_size metrics (ENG-4875 / redwood PR#19188). Target by 12/12.
- [Hiro + Omar] Kernel tagging: add kernel_id + selection version tag (ENG-4876 / redwood PR#19193). Target by 12/12.
- [Logan + Allison] Metric label set + histogram strategy review; produce “allowed labels” list (cardinality audit memo). Target by 12/11.
- [Nadia] Baseline store proposal: artifact location, schema, versioning, update policy (ENG-4874). Target by 12/13.
- [Allison + Rafael] Draft warning alert rules + incident-bot payload (ENG-4878). Target by 12/16.
- [Connor + Marissa] Define rollout gate behavior (pause/rollback criteria) for phase 2; initial spec in PM-642. Target by 12/18.

Risks / watchouts
- Baseline drift + fleet changes causing alert storms.
- Telemetry ingestion latency causing late alerts (confusing because observed window != baseline window).
- Cardinality blowups (kernel_id or model_version too granular).
- Canary overhead creeping up if model count grows without caps.

Notes to self (Noah)
- Keep MVP small; get signal quality right before expanding.
- Do not let this turn into a giant benchmarking suite; it’s a canary + fast triage.
- Ensure “disable switch” exists and is documented for oncall.

Decision log (start)
- 2025-12-02: MVP will be synthetic prompts only; no customer prompt shadowing (agreed).
- 2025-12-02: Start us-east only; 2–3 models; warning-only at first (agreed).
- TBD: Baseline strategy (fixed vs rolling) + exact alert thresholds.
